questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The city's offers and the university

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The communication from uLisboa was not perfect, but I managed to get the info I needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: E-mails about the welcome session and then information at the school.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The selection of classes was very messy, it happened during the first week and seemed to come as a surprise to most professors. The process was pretty confusing, but I managed fine.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was fine.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Of course it entails longer transportation time and probably higher rent, but it's definitely nice in the sense that you get to experience the city more locally.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I ticked off the option to be informed about student housing, but I never heard anything from uLisboa about this.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Again, the process of selecting classes was messy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We came to the welcome session, received our student cards and then we selected classes the following week.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was an international office and an e-mail you could write, which I did. The response time was often a bit long, but otherwise it was ok.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 3/5 that I initially wanted, and the remaining 2 were also subjects that I ended up enjoying. Many of my classmates however had more trouble than me getting enrolled.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient and try to remain calm during the process. It was fine for me.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All my 5 courses seemed to be introduction classes for 1st year students. The level was pretty different from what I'm used to at uCPH, the amount of reading was completely absent in some classes, the method of teaching also pretty different. Overall, my experience was good in most classes, but the academic level was definitely way lower.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was all class-based, participating in class was important, the method of learning was more focused on memorizing information and being able to showcase this in the final written tests.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I was enrolled in: The Study of The Human Language, Elements for a Music History of the 20th Century, Classical Culture, The Study of Cultures and Language & Communication.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all except The Study of Cultures. The professor was unprofessional, didn't plan his courses properly and I didn't learn anything from this course.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The cost of living was pretty cheap in Lisbon.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't use them.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They offered different kinds, but I didn't make use of them.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I mostly socialized and explored the city outside of the school.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There's a lot of stuff to do! In the weekend, you can go to the beach in Cascais or Carcavelos, you can plan a day trip to Sintra to see the castle and the park, you can go to the south of Portugal with the train for a couple of days, take a couple of days in Porto (cheap and fast with flixbus) or explore nearby places such as Madeira, The Azores, Spain, Morocco etc (a bit expensive of course). Otherwise just exploring Lisbon by foot, trying the food, going vintage hunting, visiting museums and the various charming parks with friends!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I was mostly paired with other international students in my English taught classes. I socialized with locals by attending dance classes, which was nice.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None. But I would recommend enrolling in the Portuguese classes that uLisboa offers, I didn't but wish I did. They take up some time, as they're held during the evening a couple of days per week.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The locals are super sweet, the food (fish) is amazing, the vibe of the city is generally really nice. A lot of life during both the day and night.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Try to learn portuguese (I didn't)
- Don't be hesitant to join activities outside school (like dance, training etc) --> it helps you get a nice routine 
- Travel more around Portugal than I did. Getting around with bus and train is easy and pretty cheap.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware that the academic level of the classes is pretty different than here in Copenhagen, but if you adjust to the philosophy of teaching, you can still benefit a lot from the classes.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know a lot of sweet people and establishing a relationship to the city of Lisbon.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I didn't have a lot of challenges, so I can't really think of any.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: nope

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
